p.src: Now Baoyu, seeing that the outer study had been put in order, arranged to read there at night with Qin Zhong. But Qin Zhong was frail by nature. After exposure to wind and frost in the countryside and his secret, passionate trysts with Zhineng, he had inevitably neglected his health. On returning, he caught a cold and began coughing, lost his appetite, and seemed quite unable to bear up; therefore, he dared not go out and remained at home recuperating. Baoyu's pleasure was thus spoiled, but there was nothing he could do; he could only wait quietly until Qin Zhong had fully recovered before arranging another meeting.

p.src: By then Xifeng had received Yun Guang's reply, and everything had been settled. The old nun informed the Zhang family, and the garrison commander did indeed swallow his anger and accept the former betrothal gifts back. Who would have thought that parents as greedy for wealth and influence as the Zhangs had raised a daughter so loving and honorable? When she learned that they had broken off her former engagement, she quietly hanged herself with a hempen rope. When the commander's son heard that Jinge had hanged herself, being deeply devoted himself, he too threw himself into a river and died, remaining faithful to his betrothed. The Zhang and Li families were left humiliated, having lost both their children and their wealth. Xifeng, meanwhile, sat back and pocketed three thousand taels, while Lady Wang and the others knew nothing whatsoever about it. From then on Xifeng grew ever bolder, and whenever such matters arose afterward, she began acting entirely as she pleased. There is no need to record any more of this.

p.src: One day, on Jia Zheng's birthday, the members of both the Ning and Rong households assembled to celebrate, creating a scene of extraordinary bustle and festivity. Suddenly a gatekeeper hurried in and reported before the banquet, “His Lordship Xia, Chief Eunuch of the Six Palaces, has come to deliver an imperial command.” Jia She, Jia Zheng, and the rest were so alarmed, not knowing what the news might be, that they hastily stopped the opera, cleared away the feast, set out an incense table, opened the central gate, and knelt to receive the command. Presently they saw Xia Shouzhong, Chief Eunuch of the Six Palaces, arrive on horseback, attended on every side by numerous palace eunuchs. Xia Shouzhong carried neither edict nor rescript. Dismounting beneath the eaves, he walked into the hall with a broad smile, stood facing south, and announced, “By special imperial command: Jia Zheng is to enter the palace immediately and appear before His Majesty in the Linjing Hall.” Having said this, he left on horseback without even waiting for tea. Jia She and the others had no idea what this might portend. They could only hurry to change their clothes and enter the palace.

p.src: Grandmother Jia and the whole family were filled with anxious uncertainty and constantly sent horsemen back and forth for news. After about four hours, Lai Da and three or four other stewards suddenly came panting through the ceremonial gate with congratulations, saying, “Master has ordered that the Old Lady quickly lead the ladies into the palace to give thanks for imperial favor.” At that moment Grandmother Jia, still distraught, was standing beneath the veranda of the great hall. Lady Xing, Lady Wang, Madam You, Li Wan, Xifeng, Yingchun and her sisters, Aunt Xue, and the others were all gathered there. On hearing this report, Grandmother Jia summoned Lai Da and questioned him closely about what had happened. Lai Da replied, “We servants were waiting outside the Linjing Gate and could learn nothing at all about what was happening inside. Later, Eunuch Xia came out and congratulated us, saying that our family's eldest young lady had been elevated to Director of the Phoenix Algae Palace and additionally ennobled as Consort of Worthy Virtue. When Master came out afterward, he gave us the same instructions. Master has now gone on to the Eastern Palace, so the Old Lady is requested to lead the ladies quickly into the palace to give thanks for imperial favor.” Only after hearing this did Grandmother Jia and the others feel reassured, and naturally their faces now shone with overflowing joy. They then dressed in full ceremonial attire appropriate to their ranks. Grandmother Jia led Lady Xing, Lady Wang, and Madam You to the palace in four large sedan chairs. Jia She and Jia Zhen also changed into court dress and, taking Jia Rong and Jia Qiang with them, escorted Grandmother Jia's sedan chair on its way. Thus, throughout both the Ning and Rong households, high and low, inside and out, everyone was jubilant. Each face wore an air of triumph, and the clamor of talk and laughter never ceased.

p.src: Meanwhile, Zhineng had recently fled secretly from Water-Moon Convent into the city and gone to Qin Zhong's home to visit him. Qin Ye unexpectedly discovered her, drove her out, and gave Qin Zhong a beating. In his fury, his chronic illness flared up, and within three or five days he breathed his last. Qin Zhong was already weak and had not recovered from his illness. After being beaten, he now saw that his aged father had died of anger; his remorse and anguish came too late, and many further symptoms afflicted him. Because of this, Baoyu felt desolate, as though he had lost something precious. Even hearing of Yuanchun's elevation did nothing to dispel his melancholy. How Grandmother Jia and the others gave thanks for imperial favor and returned home, how friends and relatives came to offer congratulations, how lively the Ning and Rong households had lately become, and how delighted everyone was—he alone regarded it all as though it were nothing and paid it no attention whatsoever. For this reason everyone teased him for having grown even more foolish. Fortunately, word arrived ahead of Jia Lian and Daiyu that they were returning and would reach home the next day. Only on hearing this did Baoyu show a little happiness. On asking the details, he learned that Jia Yucun too was coming to the capital for an imperial audience. Wang Ziteng had repeatedly submitted memorials recommending him, and he was now to await appointment to a vacancy in the capital. Since he and Jia Lian belonged to the same clan, while he had also been Daiyu's tutor, they had traveled together as companions. Lin Ruhai had been buried in the ancestral graveyard, and only after all affairs had been properly settled did Jia Lian set out for the capital. They should originally have reached home after the end of the month, but on hearing the joyful news about Yuanchun, they hastened onward day and night; all had remained safe throughout the journey. Baoyu cared only to hear the two words “Daiyu is safe”; nothing else concerned him.

p.src: After what seemed an endless wait, noon came the next day, and sure enough someone reported, “Second Master Lian and Miss Lin have entered the residence.” When they met, sorrow and joy mingled in every heart. Inevitably, they wept bitterly for a time, and afterward exchanged words of congratulation. As Baoyu quietly appraised Daiyu, he thought she had grown even more ethereally graceful. Daiyu had also brought many books. She busied herself with cleaning her room and arranging its furnishings, then distributed some paper, brushes, and other articles among Baochai, Yingchun, Baoyu, and the others. Baoyu carefully took out the fragrant wagtail-bead bracelet given to him by the Prince of Beijing and presented it in turn to Daiyu. Daiyu said, “Something some foul man has handled! I do not want it.” With that, she tossed it aside and refused to take it. Baoyu had no choice but to take it back. For the moment, there is nothing more to tell.

p.src: Now Jia Lian, after returning home and paying his respects to everyone, went back to his own rooms. Xifeng had lately been overwhelmed with affairs and had not a moment to spare, but since Jia Lian had returned from his long journey, she naturally had to set aside her work to receive him. With no outsiders in the room, she smiled and said, “Congratulations, my lord and Imperial Brother-in-law! You must be weary and travel-stained after your journey, my lord. This humble servant heard from the first courier yesterday that Your Excellency would return to the residence today, so I have prepared a modest cup of wine to wash away the dust of the road. Might you deign to honor me by accepting it?” “I would hardly dare! You are too kind, too kind,” Jia Lian replied with a laugh. Meanwhile, Ping’er and the other maids finished paying their respects and served him tea. Jia Lian then asked about everything that had happened in the household during his absence and thanked Xifeng for all her hard work in managing it. “How could I possibly manage all those affairs?” said Xifeng. “My understanding is shallow, my tongue is clumsy, and I am so simplehearted that if someone hands me a cudgel, I take it for a needle. “I am softhearted too; a couple of pleasant words are enough to melt my heart. “Besides, I have never handled any great affair and am timid by nature. If Her Ladyship feels even slightly unwell, I become so frightened that I cannot sleep. “Several times I earnestly begged to be excused, but Her Ladyship would not allow it. Instead, she accused me of seeking an easy life and refusing to learn. “Little does she know that I have been in a cold sweat the whole time. “I dare not say one word too many or take one step too far. “You know what all those housekeeper-wives in our family are like. Is there a single one who is easy to deal with? “Make the slightest mistake and they laugh and jeer at you; show the least partiality and they complain by abusing the mulberry while pointing at the locust tree. “Sitting on the hill to watch the tigers fight, killing with a borrowed sword, fanning the wind to spread the fire, standing safely on dry ground, and refusing to right an overturned oil jar—they are masters of the whole repertoire. “And since I am young and lack the seniority to command respect, I can hardly blame them for disregarding me. “More absurd still, when Rong’s wife suddenly died over at the other residence, Cousin Zhen repeatedly knelt before Her Ladyship and begged her to let me help him for a few days. I refused again and again, but Her Ladyship absolutely would not hear of it, so I had no choice but to obey. “As usual, I threw everything into utter confusion and made a complete disgrace of it. Even now Cousin Zhen is still complaining and regretting that he asked me. “Now that you are back, when you see him tomorrow, please smooth things over for me. Tell him I am young and have never seen much of the world, and that it was his own fault for entrusting the task to the wrong person.” As she was speaking, voices were heard in the outer room. “Who is that?” Xifeng asked. Ping’er came in and replied, “Aunt Xue sent young Xiangling to ask me something. I have answered her and sent her back.”

p.src: “Ah, yes,” Jia Lian said with a laugh. “Just now, when I went to see Aunt Xue, I unexpectedly came face-to-face with a young woman. She was remarkably good-looking. “I could not recall anyone like her in our household, so while speaking with Aunt Xue I asked who she was. It turned out she was Xiangling, the little maid bought on the journey to the capital. She has now become that big fool Xue’s chamber woman; since having her face threaded, she has grown even more strikingly beautiful. “That great fool Xue is truly unworthy of her.” “Oh, honestly!” exclaimed Xifeng. “After a journey through Suzhou and Hangzhou, you ought to have broadened your horizons, yet you are still as greedy-eyed as ever, though your belly is already full. “If you fancy her, that is easily arranged. Shall I go and exchange Ping’er for her? “Master Xue is another man who eats from his bowl while eyeing the pot. For nearly a year, because he wanted Xiangling but could not have her, he made no end of trouble for Aunt Xue. “Aunt Xue did not merely think Xiangling pretty; she saw that her character and conduct were unlike those of other girls. She was gentle and quiet, and even many young ladies of good families could not compare with her. So Aunt Xue went to the trouble of giving a banquet and inviting guests, and formally made her his concubine. “Yet before half a month had passed, he treated her as no more than a puff of wind through a stable. I cannot help feeling sorry for her.” Before she had finished speaking, a page from the inner gate announced, “The Master is waiting for Second Master in the main study.” Hearing this, Jia Lian hurriedly straightened his clothes and went out.

p.src: Xifeng then asked Ping’er, “What business did Aunt Xue have just now, that she specially sent Xiangling here?” “There was no Xiangling,” Ping’er replied with a smile. “I merely borrowed her name to tell a lie for the moment. “Just think, Mistress—Wang’er’s wife has become more thoughtless than ever.” As she spoke, she went over to Xifeng and whispered, “Of all times to bring the interest money, she neither brought it later nor earlier, but chose to deliver it now, when Second Master is at home. “Fortunately, I ran into her in the main room. Otherwise, if she had come in to report to you and Second Master had asked what interest money it was, you would naturally have refused to conceal it from him and would have had to tell him the truth. “You know Second Master’s temperament: he would fish coins out of a boiling oil pot to spend them. If he learned that you had this private hoard, he would not rest until he had spent it too. “So I hurried to take the money from her and gave her a scolding. But you happened to hear us and asked who it was, so I lied and said Xiangling had come.” Xifeng laughed. “I thought it strange! Knowing that your Second Master had returned, why would Aunt Xue suddenly send one of her nephew’s chamber women here? “So it was you, you little minx, playing your tricks!”

p.src: As they were speaking, Jia Lian came in, and Xifeng ordered wine and food to be served so that husband and wife might sit opposite each other. Though Xifeng could hold her liquor, she did not dare drink freely and merely kept Jia Lian company. Presently Jia Lian's wet nurse, Nanny Zhao, came in. Jia Lian and Xifeng hastened to offer her wine and invited her onto the kang. Nanny Zhao firmly refused. Pinger and the others had already placed a stool below the edge of the kang, together with a small footstool, and Nanny Zhao sat down on the footstool. Jia Lian selected two dishes from the table, set them on the stool for her, and told her to help herself. Xifeng said, “Mother can hardly chew that. It will only hurt her teeth.” Then she said to Pinger, “This morning I told you that bowl of ham-stewed pork knuckle was very tender and just right for Mother. Why didn't you take it and have them heat it up at once?” She added, “Mother, taste the Huiquan wine your son brought back.” Nanny Zhao said, “I'll drink, but you should have a cup too, madam. What is there to fear? Just do not drink too much. I did not come rushing over now for the wine; there is a serious matter I want you to keep in mind, madam, and I beg you to look after me. Our master is full of fine words, but when the time comes, he forgets all about us. And to think that I nursed you from infancy until you were this big! I am old now, and all I have are those two sons. If you would show them special favor and look after them, no one else would dare utter a word against it. I have begged you again and again; you always promised readily enough, but to this day nothing has come of it. Now this great piece of good fortune has suddenly fallen from heaven—surely plenty of hands will be needed? That is why I thought it more sensible to speak to you, madam. If I depended on our master, I fear I might starve to death.”

p.src: Xifeng laughed. “Don't worry, Mother. Entrust both my foster brothers to me. You nursed your son from infancy; surely you know his temperament better than anyone. He takes what belongs to his own flesh and blood and lavishes it on complete outsiders. When his own foster brothers are right here, which of them is not as capable as anyone else? If he favored and looked after them, who would dare say no? There is no reason to let outsiders reap all the benefits. But perhaps I have said that wrongly. They may be ‘outsiders’ to us, but to you they are just like ‘insiders’—your own intimate friends.” At this, everyone in the room burst out laughing. Nanny Zhao too laughed without stopping and invoked the Buddha. “At last a clear-sighted judge has appeared in this household! As for all that nonsense about ‘insiders’ and ‘outsiders,’ our master has no such motives. He is merely tenderhearted and kind, and cannot withstand a few words of pleading.” Xifeng laughed. “Exactly! I shall have another cup of this fine wine. Now that our madam has taken charge, I have nothing left to worry about.”

u.src: Xifeng laughed. “Don't worry, Mother. Entrust both my foster brothers to me.
You nursed your son from infancy; surely you know his temperament better than anyone.
He takes what belongs to his own flesh and blood and lavishes it on complete outsiders.
When his own foster brothers are right here, which of them is not as capable as anyone else?
If he favored and looked after them, who would dare say no?
There is no reason to let outsiders reap all the benefits.
But perhaps I have said that wrongly. They may be ‘outsiders’ to us, but to you they are just like ‘insiders’—your own intimate friends.”
At this, everyone in the room burst out laughing.
Nanny Zhao too laughed without stopping and invoked the Buddha. “At last a clear-sighted judge has appeared in this household!
As for all that nonsense about ‘insiders’ and ‘outsiders,’ our master has no such motives. He is merely tenderhearted and kind, and cannot withstand a few words of pleading.”

p.src: Jia Lian was embarrassed by now. He merely drank with an awkward smile and muttered, “Nonsense!” Then he called, “Hurry and serve the rice. After a bowl I must go over to Cousin Zhen's place to discuss some business.” Xifeng said, “Indeed, you must not delay important business. What did Master summon you for just now?” “It was about the imperial visit home,” replied Jia Lian. Xifeng asked quickly, “Has the imperial visit home actually been approved?” Jia Lian laughed. “It is not completely certain, but it is eighty percent certain.” Xifeng smiled. “That shows the boundless grace of His Present Majesty. In all the tales we have heard and plays we have seen, nothing like it ever happened in ancient times.” Nanny Zhao joined in again. “Quite so. I must be muddleheaded in my old age. For days I have heard everyone, high and low, making a commotion about some imperial visit home, but I paid no attention. Now you speak of it again—what exactly is it all about?” Jia Lian said, “His Present Majesty now shows the utmost consideration for the hearts of all his people. Nothing in the world is greater than filial piety, and the natural bond between parents and children is surely the same for all, with no distinction between noble and humble. His Majesty himself serves the Retired Emperor and the Empress Dowager day and night, yet still feels unable to fulfill his filial devotion even in the smallest measure. Seeing that the imperial consorts and court ladies have all spent many years in the palace, separated from the sight and voices of their parents, how could they not long for them? It is only right and proper that children should miss their parents. And if parents at home continually long for their daughters but can never see them, and consequently fall ill or even die, it is because We have confined the daughters and prevented them from fulfilling the natural desires of family affection; this too would gravely offend the harmony of Heaven. He therefore memorialized the Retired Emperor and the Empress Dowager, proposing that on every date containing a two or a six, the relatives of the palace ladies be permitted to enter the palace, pay their respects, and visit them. The Retired Emperor and the Empress Dowager were delighted and warmly praised His Majesty for his supreme filial devotion, pure benevolence, accord with Heaven, and understanding of all things. The two venerable sovereigns then issued a further decree, observing that when the families of palace ladies entered the palace, the formalities prescribed by imperial dignity were unavoidable, so mothers and daughters still could not fully satisfy their affection. They therefore extended an extraordinary favor and specially decreed to the noble families connected with the imperial consorts that, in addition to the privilege of entering the palace on dates containing a two or a six, any household possessing spacious residences and separate gardens suitable for receiving the imperial procession and establishing the necessary security might petition for the imperial carriage to visit its private estate, so that the natural affection between flesh and blood might find some measure of fulfillment. Once this decree was issued, who could fail to rejoice and give grateful praise? At this very moment, the father of Honored Lady Zhou has already begun construction at home and is building a separate residence for her imperial visit. And the household of Wu Tianyou, father of Imperial Consort Wu, has also gone outside the city to inspect possible sites. Does that not make it eighty or ninety percent certain?”

p.src: Nanny Zhao exclaimed, “Amitabha! So that is how it is. Then our family must also prepare to welcome our eldest young lady home?” Jia Lian replied, “Of course! What else do you suppose all this bustle is about?” Xifeng laughed. “If that is really so, I shall witness a truly magnificent spectacle. It is a pity I was born a few years too late. Had I been born twenty or thirty years earlier, these old people could no longer look down on me for knowing nothing of the great world. The tales they tell of how the Founding Emperor toured the realm in imitation of Shun are livelier than a whole book, yet I had no luck to be there.” Nanny Zhao cried, “Oh, that was a sight one might not encounter in a thousand years! I was only just old enough to remember things then. Our Jia household was supervising the construction of seagoing vessels and repairing the sea walls around Suzhou and Yangzhou, all to prepare for a single imperial visit, and the silver flowed away like seawater! Speaking of that...” Xifeng hastily cut in, “Our Wang household prepared for one as well. At that time my grandfather alone was responsible for the tribute and congratulations offered by all the foreign states, and whenever foreigners came, our household maintained them all. All the foreign ships and goods in Guangdong, Fujian, Yunnan, and Zhejiang belonged to our family.”

p.src: Nanny Zhao said, “Who does not know that? Even now there is a saying: ‘When the Eastern Sea lacks a bed of white jade, the Dragon King appeals to the Wang of Jiangnan.’ That refers precisely to your ladyship’s family. And then there is the Zhen family now in Jiangnan—oh, what magnificence! Their family alone received the imperial procession four times. Had we not seen it with our own eyes, no one would believe us if we told them. Never mind that silver was treated like common dirt; everything under heaven was piled there in mountains and heaped up like the sea, until no one had a thought left for the words ‘sinful waste.’” Xifeng said, “I have often heard our elders say the same, so of course I believe it. I only wonder how their family came to be so enormously rich and exalted.” Nanny Zhao replied, “Let me tell your ladyship the truth: they merely spent the Emperor’s own silver upon the Emperor! What private household could afford so much money merely to purchase that hollow splendor?” While the conversation was at its liveliest, Lady Wang again sent someone to see whether Xifeng had finished eating. Xifeng knew that some matter awaited her, so she hurriedly ate half a bowl of rice, rinsed her mouth, and was about to leave when pages from the inner gate reported, “Young Masters Rong and Qiang from the Eastern Mansion have arrived.” Jia Lian had just rinsed his mouth, and Pinger was holding a basin for him to wash his hands. When he saw the two enter, he asked, “What is it? Out with it.” Xifeng stopped and waited a moment to hear what the two had come to report. Jia Rong spoke first. “My father sent me to report to you, Uncle: the masters have settled upon a plan. Beginning with the garden of the Eastern Mansion along the eastern side and extending around to the north, the measured site is three and a half li in all, enough to build a separate residence for the imperial homecoming. Someone has already been ordered to draw up the plans, which should be ready tomorrow. As you have only just returned home and must be tired, there is no need to come over to our side tonight. They will invite you over early tomorrow morning to discuss the details in person.” Jia Lian hastily replied with a smile, “Many thanks to the master for his thoughtful consideration. I shall not come over tonight. That plan really will save trouble and make the building easier. If we were to purchase a site elsewhere, it would cause still more trouble and would not form a proper whole. Go back and say that this arrangement is excellent. If the masters should wish to alter it again, we must rely on the master to dissuade them; on no account should they seek another site. Early tomorrow morning I shall call upon the master to pay my respects, and then we can discuss the particulars.” Jia Rong promptly answered “Yes” several times.

p.src: Jia Qiang then stepped forward and reported, “For the journey to Suzhou to engage instructors, purchase girls, and procure musical instruments, costumes, and other necessities, the master has appointed me. I am to take with me two sons of Steward Lai, as well as Shan Pinren and Bu Guxiu, the two literary retainers. That is why he ordered me to come and see you, Uncle.” Hearing this, Jia Lian looked Jia Qiang up and down, then asked with a smile, “Are you capable in this line of work? Though the business is not especially great, there are many hidden intricacies in it.” Jia Qiang smiled. “I can only learn as I go and do my best.”

p.src: Standing beside Xifeng in the lamplight, Jia Rong secretly tugged at her robe. Understanding his meaning, Xifeng laughed and said, “You worry far too much. Do you imagine the master knows less about choosing men than we do? And yet you have to fear that he is inexperienced. Who begins as an expert? The boys are grown now, and even if they have never eaten pork, they have at least seen a pig run. The master is sending him merely as a figurehead. Surely he does not seriously expect the boy himself to bargain over prices and conduct the business! In my opinion, the arrangement is excellent.” “Naturally,” said Jia Lian. I was not rejecting the proposal; I merely had to think matters through on his behalf.” He then asked, “From which account is the money for this to be drawn?” Jia Qiang answered, “We were discussing that just now. Old Steward Lai said there is no need to carry the money down from the capital, since the Zhen family in Jiangnan is still holding fifty thousand taels of our silver. Tomorrow they will write a letter and draft for us to take along. We shall draw thirty thousand taels first and leave the remaining twenty thousand on deposit to cover the cost of candles, decorative lanterns, and all kinds of curtains, screens, and hangings.” Jia Lian nodded. “That is a good plan.”

p.src: Xifeng promptly said to Jia Qiang, “In that case, I have two capable and reliable men whom you can take along to handle the business. That will make things easy for you.” Jia Qiang hastily smiled ingratiatingly. “I was just about to ask you, Aunt, to lend me two men. What fortunate timing!” He asked their names. Xifeng turned to ask Nanny Zhao. By then Nanny Zhao had become so absorbed in listening that she sat in a daze. Pinger laughingly nudged her, and only then did she come to herself and hastily say, “One is called Zhao Tianliang, and the other Zhao Tiandong.” Xifeng said, “Do not forget. I must be off about my own business.” With that, she went out. Jia Rong hurried after her to see her out, then whispered, “If there is anything you want, Aunt, tell me and I shall make out a list for Cousin Qiang to take with him, so that he can purchase everything according to it.” Xifeng laughed. “Stop farting through your mother’s mouth! I already have more belongings than I know where to put. Do you think I covet your furtive little dealings?” And with that, she went straight on her way.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jia Qiang quietly asked Jia Lian, “Is there anything you would like? I can have it woven while I am there and present it to you.” Jia Lian laughed. “Do not get carried away. You have only just begun learning how to conduct business, yet you have already learned this little trick. If I find myself in need of anything, I shall naturally write and tell you. Let us say no more about it here.” With that, he dismissed the two of them. Afterward, people came three or four times and more to report on business. Jia Lian grew tired and sent word to the inner gate that no further reports were to be brought in; everything was to wait until the next day. It was not until the third watch that Xifeng was finally able to retire. Nothing further happened that night.

p.src: Early the next morning, Jia Lian rose, paid his respects to Jia She and Jia Zheng, and went to the Ning mansion. Together with the senior stewards, several family friends, retainers, and gentlemen of leisure, he surveyed the grounds of both mansions and drew up plans for the halls where the Imperial Consort would be received, while also estimating and arranging the labor required. From then on, craftsmen of every trade assembled, while gold, silver, copper, tin, earth, timber, bricks, tiles, and other materials were carried back and forth without cease. The craftsmen were first ordered to demolish the walls and pavilions of the Ning mansion’s Garden of Gathered Fragrance, opening it directly into the great eastern courtyard of the Rong mansion. All the rows of servants’ quarters on the eastern side of the Rong mansion had already been torn down. Although a narrow lane had formerly separated the Ning and Rong residences, preventing passage between them, it too was private property rather than a public thoroughfare, so the two estates could be joined. The Garden of Gathered Fragrance already drew a stream of running water from beneath the wall at its northern corner, so there was no need to channel in another. Though its rocks and trees were insufficient, Jia She lived in the Rong mansion’s old garden, whose bamboo, trees, ornamental rocks, pavilions, balustrades, and other features could all be moved over. Since the two places were also very close, combining them saved a great deal of money and labor; and even if the materials still fell short, only a limited amount would have to be added. They owed everything to an experienced master designer known as Shanziye, who planned every detail of the construction.

p.src: Jia Zheng was unaccustomed to practical affairs and left all arrangements to Jia She, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, Lai Da, Lai Sheng, Lin Zhixiao, Wu Xindeng, Zhan Guang, Cheng Rixing, and the others. As for heaping up hills, digging ponds, raising towers and pavilions, planting bamboo and flowers, and arranging all the scenic features, these too were designed by Shanziye. In his leisure after returning from court, Jia Zheng merely made the rounds to inspect the work and discussed the most important points with Jia She and the others; that was all. Jia She remained at home reclining at his ease. If even the smallest matter arose, Jia Zhen and the others either went to report it in person or wrote a brief memorandum; whenever there were instructions to convey, Jia Lian, Lai Da, and the rest were summoned to receive them. Jia Rong was placed solely in charge of having the gold and silver vessels made. Jia Qiang had already set out for Gusu. Jia Zhen, Lai Da, and the others selected workmen, opened registers, supervised the construction, and attended to countless other matters impossible to recount stroke by stroke; suffice it to say that the bustle and clamor were extraordinary. For the time being, there is nothing more to tell of this.

p.src: Now Baoyu was delighted that, with such momentous affairs occupying the household, Jia Zheng no longer questioned him about his studies. Yet Qin Zhong’s illness worsened day by day, causing him such genuine anxiety that he could take pleasure in nothing. Early one morning, just after washing and dressing, he was about to ask Grandmother Jia’s permission to visit Qin Zhong when he suddenly saw Mingyan peering furtively around the screen wall by the inner gate. Baoyu hurried out and asked, “What are you doing?” “Young Master Qin is not going to last!” said Mingyan. Baoyu started in alarm. “But I only went to see him yesterday, and he was perfectly conscious. How can he be dying already?” “I do not know either,” said Mingyan. “An old servant from his household came just now especially to tell me.” On hearing this, Baoyu hurried back to inform Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia instructed, “Make sure reliable attendants go with you. Once there, pay the respects due to a fellow student and then come straight back. You must not linger.” Baoyu hastily changed his clothes and came out, but the carriage was still not ready, and he paced anxiously about the hall. At last, after repeated urging, the carriage arrived. Baoyu hurried aboard, accompanied by Li Gui, Mingyan, and the others. When they reached Qin Zhong’s gate, not a soul was to be seen. They surged straight into the inner room, frightening Qin Zhong’s two distant aunts and several male cousins so badly that they scrambled to hide.

At last, after repeated urging, the carriage arrived. Baoyu hurried aboard, accompanied by Li Gui, Mingyan, and the others.

When they reached Qin Zhong’s gate, not a soul was to be seen. They surged straight into the inner room, frightening Qin Zhong’s two distant aunts and several male cousins so badly that they scrambled to hide.

p.src: By this time Qin Zhong had already lost consciousness two or three times, and his bed had long since been moved and its mat changed in preparation for death. At the sight, Baoyu could not keep from crying out. Li Gui hurriedly remonstrated, “You must not, you must not! Young Master Qin suffers from a wasting illness, and his bones could not bear lying stiffly on the heated brick bed, so they have moved him down for a while to make him more comfortable. If you carry on like this, young master, will you not only make his illness worse?” Hearing this, Baoyu managed to restrain himself and went closer. Qin Zhong’s face was as white as wax; his eyes were closed, and he breathed upon the pillow. Baoyu called urgently, “Brother Jing! Baoyu is here.” He called two or three times, but Qin Zhong made no response. Baoyu said again, “Baoyu is here.”

p.src: Qin Zhong's soul had already left his body, and only one faint, lingering breath remained in his breast, when he saw a host of infernal judges coming to seize him, bearing their tablets and carrying chains. Qin Zhong's soul, however, was unwilling to go. He remembered that no one was left at home to manage the household, worried about the three or four thousand taels of silver his father had saved, and fretted because Zhineng's whereabouts were still unknown. He therefore pleaded with the infernal judges in every way he could. But the infernal judges refused to show partiality and instead rebuked Qin Zhong: “And you call yourself a man who has read books! Do you not know the common saying, ‘If the King of Hell summons you to die at the third watch, who dares keep you until the fifth?’ From the highest to the lowest, we in the netherworld are sternly impartial. We are not like you in the world of the living, forever swayed by feelings and personal ties and hampered by countless considerations.” Amid this commotion, Qin Zhong's soul suddenly heard the words “Baoyu has come.” He hastened to beg them again: “Divine emissaries, please show me a little mercy and let me return. I shall say just one word to this dear friend and come straight back.” The ghosts asked, “And what dear friend might that be?” Qin Zhong replied, “I will not conceal it from you: he is the grandson of the Duke of Rongguo, and his childhood name is Baoyu.” At this, the Chief Judge was the first to take fright. He hurriedly cursed the ghostly messengers: “I told you to let him go back for a little while, but you simply would not heed me. Now you will not be satisfied until he brings forth someone blessed with flourishing fortune and ascendant power!” Seeing the Chief Judge react this way, all the ghosts grew flustered too, and complained: “A moment ago, Your Reverence was all thunderbolts and hailstones, yet it turns out that you cannot bear the mere word ‘Baoyu.’ In our humble opinion, he belongs to the realm of yang while we belong to yin; fearing such people can do us no good.” “Nonsense!” said the Chief Judge. “The proverb rightly says, ‘Officials under heaven govern all affairs under heaven.’ From ancient times, the ways of men and ghosts have been alike; the principles of yin and yang are not two. Whether he belongs to yin or yang, we cannot go wrong by letting this one return.” On hearing this, the ghosts had no choice but to release Qin Zhong's soul. With a groan, he opened his eyes slightly and, seeing Baoyu beside him, sighed with difficulty: “Why would you not come sooner? Had you been one step later, you would not have seen me at all.” Baoyu hurriedly took his hand and said through his tears, “If you have anything to say, leave me a word or two.” Qin Zhong said, “I have nothing else to say. In the past, you and I believed our understanding surpassed that of everyone else; only today do I realize how I misled myself. From now on, you should set your mind on earning rank and distinction, and make honor and advancement your proper aim.” When he had finished speaking, he gave a long sigh and quietly passed away.
